items.title: Japanese Yen futures rallied over 0.75% to a 1-month high.
items.excerpt: Japanese Yen futures rallied more than three-quarters of a percent to reach their highest levels in a month, breaking out of a tight two-week consolidation range and offsetting October selling pressure. Dan Deming of KKM Financial breaks down the primary catalysts behind the advance, highlighting Bank of Japan policy signals alongside broader safe-haven rotation driven by weakness in U.S. equity markets and buying in Treasury markets. In the broader currency space, Swiss Franc futures also demonstrated solid relative strength, while British Pound futures maintained morning gains and Euro futures edged slightly lower heading into the afternoon.

items.title: British Pound futures climb on UK inflation and rate hike expectations.
items.excerpt: British Pound futures moved higher for the fourth session in the last five, rising 1.63% since the October 14 close. Prices traded near their highest closing levels since mid-September as market expectations for a November Bank of England rate hike strengthened. UK consumer prices rose 3.5% year-over-year in September, exceeding the 3.4% forecast and accelerating from 3.1% in August, driven by a 29.8% jump in motor fuel prices and a 3.7% increase in services inflation. Additionally, UK unemployment fell to 4.7% in the three months through August, coming in below the 4.9% expectation. Interest rate markets are now pricing in a 95% probability of a rate hike to 4% on November 5, providing structural support for the currency ahead of the UK budget announcement.

items.title: CoreWeave after the bond scare: what a cash-secured put pays for, and what it carries
items.excerpt: CoreWeave shares fell about a quarter in a month as its bonds traded at distressed yields. Puts now pay more than usual. What does a cash-secured put seller get paid for, and what does the seller take on? When a company s bonds come under pressure, its puts get more expensive. The seller collects more, and takes on more. CoreWeave (CRWV on Nasdaq), which rents out computing power for AI, has had a hard month. Its shares closed at USD 62.13 on 20 October 2026, about a quarter lower than a month earlier and not far above their lowest level of the past year (Source: Saxo). Past performance is not indicative of future results. Most of the damage came on 14 October, when the shares lost more than 15% in one session. items.excerpt: Roche reports its nine-month sales on 22 October 2026, after a rise of about 9% since July. One investor wants to buy lower, another already owns the shares. How can each name a price and be paid to wait? Before a company reports, options on its shares tend to cost more than in a quiet week. Whoever sells the option collects that extra. Roche publishes its nine-month sales on Thursday 22 October 2026 at 07:00 CET, before the Swiss market opens.
